scenario.highLevelScenario: Trade Already Settled - Trade belongs to completed settlement workflow. Cancellation instruction received. Expected: NACK (trade already settled error code), no state change.
notes: Event: the trade's settlement has completed, and a cancellation instruction is then received for it. Expected: NACK with the trade already settled error code, and no state change.

One FX Spot trade is taken through the whole pipeline, and every step must pass: injection (04), both ledgers (05 / 05b), netting group (06 / 06b, 07 / 07b), close (08 / 08b), status (09 / 09b, which save the settlement ids settlementId and settlementIdB), confirmation (12 / 12b), settlement on all three sides (13, 13b, 13c), MT910 funding call (14) and both settlement ledgers at SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE (15 / 15b). The trade itself is never cancelled: no 04 cancel, 05ct_a or 05ct_b.
Steps 10, 11 and 11b follow the netting rule: the BNKA-NY / BNKB-NY FxSpot rule in data/trade_scenarios.py is auto, so they are skipped and reported as not run. Were it manual, they would run.

"cancelSettlement" with "after": "15b" then cancels the completed settlement: steps 13cs_a and 13cs_b POST .../settlement/<settlementId>/cancel on Domain A and .../<settlementIdB>/cancel on Domain B, straight after step 15b.

Its "expect" declares both fail: the cancel must be refused (the NACK), so each returns a non-2xx status and its test_cancel_returns_2xx fails. Those declared failures are written into the HTML report as passed and do not count against the exit code. If either step PASSES, the runner turns it into a failure, because a completed settlement was cancelled.

expect is per step, not per check, so a 13cs step that fails its pre-flight (no token or settlement id in state) is recorded as passed as well; steps 09 to 15b would then have failed, so the run still fails.
The cancel is declared refused, so steps 15cs_a and 15cs_b, which wait for the settlement to show CANCELLED, are not run.

Not checked: the NACK's error code (13cs_a / 13cs_b check only that the status is not 2xx), and that the settlement is still SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE after the refused cancel (no step reads the ledger again after it).
Order in the run and the report: 01, 04, 05, 05b, 06, 06b, 07, 07b, 08, 08b, 09, 09b, 10 (not run), 11 (not run), 11b (not run), 12, 12b, 13, 13b, 13c, 14, 15, 15b, 13cs_a, 13cs_b.
The cancel steps are in the HTML report only: they have no Excel column.

The sheet gives the settlement / valuation date as a past date with a completed settlement. A trade valued in the past would not settle in the run, so the current date is used, as {{TODAY}}, and steps 13 to 15b complete its settlement before the cancel is sent. The sheet's trade date is a date picker, so the run date is used. Both resolve from the run clock.

The sheet states the trade as base USD, reference CNH. It is carried as CNHUSD, the order the rest of the pack, TradeServ and the netting rule use, with each amount kept on its own currency. The sheet gives no amounts, so the pack's standard 6740 CNH (baseCurrencyAmount), 1000 USD (referenceCurrencyAmount) and rate 2 are used.

direction and Against list both options in the sheet (Buy/Sell, Base/Reference). The first of each, Buy and Base, is used, matching the rest of the pack: BNKA-NY is the base currency buyer, partyDirection Buy.
tradeReference, tradeReferenceSupplement and counterpartyReferenceNumber are free-text boxes, so they are generated per run as tradeId, the party partyTradeId and the counterparty partyTradeId.

ccpAlias, clearingBroker and counterpartyClearingBroker have no wrapper field, so they are left out of the payload entirely. Party CCP and Cpty CCP are not given in the sheet; the payload carries the ordinary PVP settlement flag.
settlementCcy (USD) has no field in the wrapper, so it is recorded here only.
